question_text:
The internet speed is measured at 6 pm at three exchanges in a particular area.

| Location | Internet speed (Mbps) |
| :---: | :---: |
| A | 44.3 |
| B | 42.7 |
| C | 45.9 |

Use nearest neighbour interpolation to estimate the internet speed at 6 pm at:

mark_breakdown.desc: Correctly states the speed estimate is $42.7\text{ Mbps}$ as $(12, 16)$ is closest to B

subparts.solution: $(12, 16)$ is closest to B, so we estimate the internet speed at 6 pm to be $42.7\text{ Mbps}$ at $(12, 16)$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Nearest neighbor interpolation uses the value of the nearest site in the Voronoi diagram.
step_by_step: Identify which cell $(12, 16)$ belongs to by inspecting the diagram (cell B).
Take the internet speed measured at site B, which is $42.7\text{ Mbps}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Averaging values instead of taking the nearest neighbor's value when the point is clearly inside one cell.

mark_breakdown.desc: Recognizing the point is on the edge between A and C and taking the mean of speeds at A and C

subparts.solution: $(-20, -12)$ is on the edge equidistant from A and C, so we estimate the internet speed at 6 pm to be $\frac{44.3 + 45.9}{2} = 45.1\text{ Mbps}$ at $(-20, -12)$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: If a point lies on an edge between two cells, it is equidistant to both sites, so the estimated value is the mean of the values of the two sites.
step_by_step: Identify that $(-20, -12)$ lies on the Voronoi edge separating cell A and cell C.
Take the internet speeds at A ($44.3\text{ Mbps}$) and C ($45.9\text{ Mbps}$).
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using values from an unrelated site (such as B).

mark_breakdown.desc: Recognizing the point is a Voronoi vertex equidistant from A, B, and C and taking the mean of all three

subparts.solution: $(-4, 4)$ is the vertex equidistant from A, B, and C, so we estimate the internet speed at 6 pm to be $\frac{44.3 + 42.7 + 45.9}{3} = 44.3\text{ Mbps}$ at $(-4, 4)$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: If a point is a Voronoi vertex, it is equidistant to the three adjacent sites, so the estimate is the mean of the values at those three sites.
step_by_step: Identify that $(-4, 4)$ is a Voronoi vertex where cells A, B, and C meet.
